answers.explanation: All mature plant cells have a cell wall made of cellulose, which gives them a rigid outer boundary.
The nucleus controls cell activities and stores genetic information, but energy is supplied by mitochondria, not the nucleus.
In ferns the sporophyte is the large, independent, dominant generation, while the gametophyte is small.
Birds build nests and feed and protect their young, which is the most developed form of parental care here.
Fish depend most on water, then frogs, then reptiles, while the least aquatic animal is the one shown as I, so the order is IV, III, II, I.
Fish are the oldest of the vertebrates shown in the diagram, which places IV as the most ancient group.
Monera are prokaryotic cells such as bacteria, which have no true nucleus, while algae and fungi are eukaryotic.
Feathers trap a layer of air, so they insulate the body and help keep heat in.
The hooked beak and strong talons of this bird are adapted for tearing and holding flesh, so it is a carnivore.
In a dicot stem the phloem lies on the outside and the xylem lies more towards the centre, so the xylem is more interiorly placed.
Xylem carries water upwards and phloem carries food in both directions, so the arrows labelled III and IV represent these movements.
Photosynthesis releases oxygen as a by-product, which is the outward movement shown by arrow II.
Kwashiorkor is caused by a severe lack of protein in the diet, which causes swelling and wasting.
Sundew and bladderwort trap and digest insects, which is holozoic feeding in addition to photosynthesis.
Benedict's solution turns from blue to brick or black-red only in the presence of a reducing sugar.
The left ventricle has the thickest muscular wall and pumps oxygenated blood to the whole body.
Systemic circulation carries blood from the heart to all body parts except the lungs.
Anaerobic respiration in yeast converts sugar into carbon(IV) oxide and alcohol.
The diaphragm is a sheet of muscle separating the thoracic cavity from the abdominal cavity.
Sebaceous glands secrete an oily substance that lubricates hair and skin and keeps them water repellent.
Bowman's capsules, where filtration takes place, lie in the outer cortex of the kidney.
Nastic responses are non-directional movements triggered by stimuli such as touch, as in the closing of Mimosa leaves.
Sperm are stored and matured in the epididymis before they are released.
Chemosynthetic organisms obtain energy by oxidising inorganic substances to make their food.
The stomach has a highly acidic content because of hydrochloric acid secreted by its walls.
Contractile vacuoles are used to remove excess water in protozoa, so IV is the correctly matched pair.
Every food chain begins with a producer, which makes food by photosynthesis.
Mycorrhizal fungi grow around plant roots and increase the absorption of inorganic ions such as phosphate from the soil.
The placenta is the organ where maternal and foetal blood come close, allowing exchange of materials while keeping the blood separate.
Erythrocytes contain haemoglobin, which has the greatest affinity for oxygen among blood components.
Dog fish live in the sea, while the other animals are land or freshwater organisms.
The two halves of the pelvic girdle meet at the pubic symphysis in front.
Nocturnal habits, burrowing and regulating internal body temperature all help desert animals cope with extreme heat.
Low rainfall, sparse vegetation and large daily temperature changes are typical of the desert biome.
Biotic factors are the living components of the environment, including organisms that affect the survival of others.
Population density is the number of individuals of a species per unit area of habitat.
Yellow fever is transmitted by the female Aedes mosquito.
Crop rotation keeps soil covered and maintains soil structure, which reduces erosion.
The malaria parasite Plasmodium falciparum is transmitted to humans by female Anopheles mosquitoes.
Tasting or not tasting phenylthiocarbamide is a clear two-class trait, so it shows discontinuous variation.
Curve III is centred between 2 and 4 m, so all its trees fall in that height range.
Plantation II has its peak at about 2 m, meaning it has the highest number of trees of about 2 m high.
Thyroxine and adrenaline are hormones that influence behaviour and activity patterns, such as the fight-or-flight response.
Each member of a pair of genes that controls a trait is called an allele.
Meiosis reduces the chromosome number from diploid (2n) to haploid (n) in the daughter cells.
From a cross of two heterozygotes (Aa x Aa), one in four offspring is recessive (aa).
In mammals the sex of an individual is determined at fertilisation, when the X or Y chromosome from the sperm combines with the egg.
Soldier termites are wingless, have a large head and strong mandibles for defence.
Whale flippers and fish fins have similar function and form but different ancestry, which is convergent evolution.
